chapter: Lawn parties, excursions and dance-hall work
title: Club excursions by train
summary: Clubs ran train excursions to Shreveport, Baton Rouge and other towns, with the band playing on the train and in pavilions, for colored crowds.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Clubs. Big clubs there in town.
Where'd they go, Chicago or Shreveport or Baton Rouge? How far?

Well, I ran a lot to Baton Rouge once. Shreveport was their first distance. That was the pride of Jeffersons. Every August, every third of August, they'd run excursions in the Shreveport. And a lot of men of longshoremen there was. They had excursions around the Lafayette, Shreveport, Morgan City, New York Barrier.
All right there. And the band would play right on the coach? Oh, yeah. Did they get a special baggage car where they'd dance or something? Or what?
No, we'd set down the seats, you know.
And where'd you put the drums?

Yeah, that fella had his drum right in the back there where you're in there on the platform. Like, you know, right in the bass. It's in the back all the time. Drumming the bass bar, you know. And we'd mostly play when we're going to hit a little town, which is going to make a stop to pick up some people. And we'd knock off a number. Until we'd get out to the place. When we'd get out to the place, well, we'd go out to the pavilion out there. And a big old pavilion, big opening place, you know. Blacker lawns. Say, like, like in New Iberia, like that, they had halls. Clubs would rent a hall out there for excursion. A lot of them had open-air places.
Would those be white clubs that would give that, or a colored club?
No, we'd want them to play for color.
It would be colored excursions? All colored excursions. How about lawn parties?
All color is good. How about lawn parties?
